P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Partly established. Exporters must repatriate export proceeds within a statutory period; sources conflict between 120 and 180 days, with penalties for overdue receivables, and a bill to replace them with a flat 20% penalty was reported. The 2019 currency law liberalised accounts: residents notify the Central Bank rather than seeking permits to open accounts abroad. Mandatory sale was not found.
P1_fx_receipts.note: Mondaq/Gratanet/UzDaily seen only via search summaries; kun.uz had an invalid TLS certificate (not bypassed) on 2026-10-22.
P1_fx_receipts.notes: Verify the current repatriation term and penalty in the Foreign Trade decree.

P2_fcy_account.answer: Reportedly yes (residents may open accounts abroad with notification only, and local FCY accounts are available), not captured.

P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Uzbekistan (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Paddle (not on its exclusion list; software sellers only, each seller reviewed); Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts); Polar (payouts); Whop (payouts); Dodo Payments (sellers); Google Play (developer registration). Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Etsy seller payments; YouTube Partner Program.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Register as an individual entrepreneur online through the Unified Portal for State Services (my.gov.uz), fo.birdarcha.uz or a Public Services Centre (One Stop Shop). Online registration often takes about two working days (IT Park, a government agency). A separate self-employed status exists for some activities (not verified here).

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: Businesses and individual entrepreneurs use the STIR (taxpayer identification number; INN in Russian). For individuals, the 14-digit PINFL (personal identification number) serves as the tax identification number (Tax Code art. 127, per LookupTax).

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents are taxed on worldwide income at a flat 12% PIT (dividends and interest 5%). Individual entrepreneurs and legal entities with annual turnover up to 12,000 BCU (threshold raised from UZS 1 billion from 1 June 2026) may opt for turnover tax, which replaces CIT and VAT and is reported monthly. From 1 January 2025 the 0% rate for exports was abolished and export income is included in the turnover-tax base. A separate self-employed regime exists (not captured).

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 12%. Turnover-tax payers (turnover up to 12,000 BCU) are outside VAT, because turnover tax replaces it. Export of goods is generally zero-rated; treatment of exported services was not captured. Foreign e-service suppliers to individuals must register for VAT. Rate confirmed by Kintsugi (2026).

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: IT Park Uzbekistan gives residents CIT and VAT exemptions and a 7.5% PIT rate on employees' salaries. Incentives run to 2040, but from 1 January 2028 they are limited to members whose IT-service exports are at least 50% of revenue. Sources conflict on whether individual freelancers can become residents: one guide describes a simplified freelancer procedure via the IT Park platform, another says only legal entities qualify. The self-employed regime is the usual alternative.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; PayPal is not available; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
